  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The
Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
SSpiroglou@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929, and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify, under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 2nd day of June 2025
at 4:00 p.m.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Beach Clean-Up

  Recommended Action: Discuss and provide feedback regarding a beach clean-up
  day to promote environmental sustainability.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou presented the staff report.

  Community Services Director Riesgo suggested holding the beach clean-up day on
  Saturday, May 31.

  Commissioner P. Lilly stated that a Saturday in late May would be ideal,
  considering events such as Mother’s Day, Prom, an orchestra field trip, and
  Memorial Day weekend.

  Chair L. Epstein stated that the City should work with Malibu High School to
  advertise community service hours.

  Commissioner K. Epstein recommended incentivizing volunteers by offering gift
  cards.

  Commissioners K. Lilly and P. Lilly stated Oaks Christian School used email blasts
  to advertise various programs and would provide the contact information to
  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou.

  Commissioner K. Epstein confirmed that Malibu High School had the Youth
  Commission recruitment in the morning announcements and Monday message.

  Commissioner Myers stated she attended private school and was the only Malibu
  resident at her school.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou stated he would contact schools to help advertise
  the Beach Clean-up Day.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission selected Saturday, May 31, 2025, for the Youth
  Commission Beach Clean-Up at Zuma Beach.

  B.  Teen Outreach

  Recommended Action: Provide feedback on teen outreach, communication, and
  marketing for Youth Commission activities.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Loquet stated Malibu High School Associated Student Body
  organized “Club Days” to market programs and events.

  Commissioner L. Epstein suggested tabling at Malibu Middle and Malibu High
  School Open Houses.

  Commissioner P. Lilly recommended attending the annual volunteer fair at Oaks
  Christian School.

  Commissioner Myers stated that emails and flyers were common forms of outreach
  at her school.

  Commissioner Porat stated that an ad could be placed in the Malibu High School
  newspaper.

  In response to Community Services Director Riesgo, Commissioner K. Epstein
  stated that Shark TV was used less frequently during the 2024-25 school year.

  Commissioner K. Lilly stated Oaks Christian School had a TV channel named Oaks
  News.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou requested that Commissioners share contacts at
  local and private schools with him.

Subject:  Commission Assignments

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the Youth Commission assignments for Fiscal
Year 2024-25; and 2) Approve assignments for Fiscal Year 2025-26 for City Council
consideration.

DISCUSSION: Each June, the Council approves Commission assignments for the
upcoming Fiscal Year. The Commission is asked to review the proposed assignments for
Fiscal Year 2025-26 (Attachment 1) to ensure alignment with the Fiscal Year 2024-25
Assignments (Attachment 2). The Commission may recommend new or revised
assignments or request edits to the proposed Fiscal Year 2025-26 assignments.

Once approved by the Commission, the recommended assignments will be taken to
Council for final approval.

ATTACHMENTS: 1) Proposed Fiscal Year 2025-26 Youth Commission Assignments
  2) Fiscal Year 2024-25 Youth Commission Assignments

  Page 1 of 1  Agenda Item # 5.A.
   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

To:  Candace Bond, Interim City Manager

From:  Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission

Date:  June 5, 2025

Re:  Recommended Youth Commission Assignments for Fiscal Year 2025-26

At its Regular meeting on June 5, 2025, the Youth Commission recommended the following be included
in its assignment in FY 2025-26:
  1.  Each Commissioner will volunteer at two City special events, which may include Tiny Tot
  Olympics, Halloween Bu Bash Carnival, Breakfast with Santa, Public Safety Fair, and/or
  Chumash Day Intertribal Gathering

  2.  Coordinate four community service-learning opportunities

  3.  Coordinate four donation-based programs that benefit non-profit organizations

  4.  Coordinate a teen health and wellness event or program to encourage physical fitness and
  mental wellness

  5.  Develop a cultural program to celebrate or bring awareness to the Chumash Native
  American Tribe

  6.  Host an informational Youth Government Summit Series with representatives from local
  government agencies and non-profit organization representatives regarding their career paths
  and job responsibilities

  7.  Promote environmental sustainability by hosting a Beach Clean-Up Day

  8.  Review opportunities for teen outreach and communication to increase attendance and
  awareness at programs and events

  9.  Review and provide feedback on City projects and programs

  10.  Make oral reports as needed to the City Council on Commission activities

  11.  Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity

  ATTACHMENT 1
   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

To:  Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission

From:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date:  June 26, 2024

Re:  Youth Commission Assignments for Fiscal Year 2024-25

At its Regular meeting on June 24, 2024, the City Council approved assignments for the Harry Barovsky
Memorial Youth Commission during Fiscal Year 2024-2025:

  1.  Each Commissioner will volunteer at two City special events; Tiny Tot Olympics, Halloween
  Bu Bash Carnival, Breakfast with Santa, and Chumash Day

  2.  Coordinate bimonthly in-person community service learning opportunities

  3.  Coordinate bimonthly donation-based programs that benefit nonprofit organizations

  4.  Coordinate a community movie night or film screening focusing on teen wellness

  5.  Host three presentations from local government agencies and non-profit organization
  representatives regarding their career path and job responsibilities

  6.  Promote environmental sustainability by hosting a Beach Clean-Up Day

  7.  Develop social media content to promote Voter Registration and participation

  8.  Review opportunities for teen outreach and communication to increase attendance and
  awareness at programs and events

  9.  Review and provide feedback on City projects and programs

  10.  Make bimonthly oral reports as needed to City Council on Commission activity

  11.  Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity

  ATTACHMENT 2

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff were working on the Malibu

  Commissioner Porat recommended combining assignments.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou stated assignment #2: Coordinate four

  environmental sustainability by hosting a Beach Clean—Up Day, could be combined

  Chair L. Epstein indicated agreement with Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou and

  In response to Commissioner Loquet, Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou stated that

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated mental health resources, in partnership
  with the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu Wellness Center, were available following

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the recruitment for the 2025-26 Youth
  Commission was higher than in previous years, and the Commission will review
  and recommend changes to the selection process.
